clue.text: Defenceless woman makes a bloomer

definitions.meaning: taken jokingly, a woman with no clothes on has nothing to shield her, an unclothed female
a flowering plant: the autumn crocus has this nickname because its flowers appear bare, without leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder (British slang for a gaffe) but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal description of an unclothed woman and the popular name for the autumn crocus.

clue.text: Fruit centre in a confection

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed or made up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Fruit at the centre of a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confection' looks like a sweet but rearranges the letters of 'centre in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is the fruit meant.

clue.text: What a rascal, not to say goodbye!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'What a rascal, not to say goodbye! (5)' for KNAVE: the only reading found is N (not) + AVE (goodbye) spoken as NAVE, with 'not' and 'goodbye' split by the indicator 'to say', which cannot be written as one sounded leaf; no source confirms the setter's parse
annotationWithheld.clue: What a rascal, not to say goodbye!

clue.text: Amputate several feet in ship's hospital?

parts.note: to dock is to cut off, as a tail
a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: A surgeon amputates several feet in a ship's sick bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' shows the definition is playful: ships go there to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where ships are built and repaired, playfully a hospital for vessels.

clue.text: UN dollar distribution for everybody

indicators.note: distribution spreads the letters out and deals them into a new order

explanation.surface: The United Nations hands out dollars to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges the letters of 'UN dollar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general and covering everyone is described as this, a synonym for comprehensive.

clue.text: Freeholders ought to be found in the country

indicators.note: to be found in places the zero inside the country

parts.note: Yemen is a country in Arabia
ought is a variant of nought, zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Landowners ought to be living in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ought' looks like 'should', but it is nought, O, which goes inside YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically these were small farmers owning their own land, freeholders.

clue.text: Problem characters in prose work

indicators.note: the letters of prose are worked, kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer finds trouble among the characters of a prose work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' says the letters of 'prose' are the material; 'work' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question that is hard to answer is called this, a synonym for a tricky problem.

clue.text: Author in a state about another

indicators.note: about means Pennsylvania goes around the second state

parts.note: Penn. is an abbreviation for Pennsylvania
MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, another state

explanation.surface: A writer living in one American state writes about another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. Penn. is an old abbreviation for Pennsylvania, so 'a state' wraps 'another' state, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer, especially one skilled at handwriting, is the meaning here.

clue.text: Gave another name to officer of privileged class

parts.note: sub is short for subaltern, a junior army officer
titled means having a noble title, aristocratic

explanation.surface: An aristocratic officer was given another name.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB, a subaltern, is a junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a secondary title, as a book's second heading, is to rename in addition.

clue.text: Applied to horsehair before removal from old Spanish nag

indicators.note: removal from says the word for before is taken out of the horse's name

parts.note: Rosinante is Don Quixote's broken-down horse
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A treatment for a horse's hair before an old Spanish nag is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The horsehair is on a violin bow. ROSINANTE, the English spelling of Don Quixote's horse, loses ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin rubbed on violin bows, strung with horsehair, to give them grip.

clue.text: Opportunity many found in church

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, used in crosswords for a large number

explanation.surface: A chance for many people to be found in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives L, the Roman fifty, standing for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir, is the example meant.

clue.text: Book to make a writer order us about

indicators.note: about means order and us are placed around the writer, enclosing it

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written
a nib is the point of a pen, the part that does the writing

explanation.surface: Instructions on producing a book: get a writer to put us in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link. OM and US are put 'about' NIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A single volume collecting several works by one author is called this kind of book.

clue.text: Imitation linen — not new!

indicators.note: not says the letter for new is to be absent from the word for linen

parts.note: napery is household linen, especially table linen

explanation.surface: Fake linen, plainly not new stock.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPERY, an old word for table linen, loses its N for 'new' through 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying in the manner of a monkey, mimicking others, is what the word means.

clue.text: Action in the theatre

parts.note: reads as a stage play's action, but means surgery done in a hospital theatre, or military action in a theatre of war

explanation.definitionFit: Surgery carried out in a hospital's theatre and a campaign in a theatre of war both take this word.

clue.text: Infallible monarch wearing modish fustian

indicators.note: wearing means the monarch has the other words on like clothes, so they surround it

parts.note: in means fashionable, modish
fustian is pompous, inflated language, which is rant
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A king who cannot err dresses in fashionable rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fustian' looks like the coarse cloth that goes with 'wearing', but it means bombast; the monarch is dressed in fashion and bombast.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from error, never mistaken, is a synonym for being incapable of fault.

clue.text: Taximeter adjustment sometimes needed to reach conclusion

indicators.note: adjustment means the letters of the word are altered, set in a new order

explanation.surface: A cab's meter sometimes needs adjusting at the end of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' rearranges 'Taximeter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A period added to a drawn match, as in football, so a result can be reached.

clue.text: These words help in investigation

parts.note: a detective's lead and the words of a crossword puzzle both help someone working something out

explanation.definitionFit: A hint that helps a detective, and the printed words a solver works from, share this name.

clue.text: Something surprising I heard before the first act

indicators.note: heard says the letter is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: the letter I, which spoken is the organ of sight
an opener is the first act on a bill

explanation.surface: Something startling I heard before the show opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I heard' gives EYE, the sound of the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that startles someone into seeing clearly is called this.

clue.text: Worn by the woman in charge behind the guns

definitions.text: Worn by the woman in charge
definitions.meaning: the bossy wife is said to wear the trousers in her household
the rear parts of gun barrels, where the shell is loaded

explanation.definitionFit: Knee-length trousers proverbially worn by the dominant partner, and the rear ends of gun barrels.

clue.text: Generosity sounds as if it gets Scrooge going

indicators.note: sounds as if says the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the name Scrooge begins with a capital, a large S

explanation.surface: Generosity seems to get a miser moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge, the miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, starts with a capital: a large S, which spoken is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal giving of money or gifts is a synonym for bounty.

clue.text: Food portion of great size

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A large serving of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'portion of' doubles as a helping of food in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for things to eat, grub.

clue.text: Go out after magazine material

indicators.note: after puts the words for go out behind the word for magazine

parts.note: an organ is a periodical publication, the mouthpiece of a group
to die is to go out, like a flame

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after picking up a fabric magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a periodical or an ammunition store; ORGAN is a society's journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, stiff, sheer cotton fabric is the kind of material meant.

clue.text: Discharge an Oriental secret

parts.note: an arc is an electric discharge between two points
taken as written
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An Eastern secret is let out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb but is an electric arc.
explanation.definitionFit: Known only to a few, mysterious, is a synonym for secret.

clue.text: Abscond, concealing city swindle

indicators.note: concealing means the word for abscond hides the city inside it

parts.note: to flee is to run away, abscond
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A fraudster absconds, hiding a city scam.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postal district.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, a synonym for swindle.

clue.text: Left in anger after square dance

indicators.note: after places the angered word behind the word for square

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: Someone left fuming after a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' puts Left inside the anger word to give RILLE, and that whole piece comes 'after' the square.
explanation.definitionFit: An old square dance for four couples, of French origin, is the kind meant.

clue.text: Blanch the bird

definitions.meaning: to blanch is to turn pale, flinch with fear
a small game bird related to the partridge

explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or cower in fear, and a small plump game bird.

clue.text: Set first stage of rocket to explode outwardly

indicators.note: outwardly means the words for explode sit on the outside, around the rocket's first letter

parts.note: to go up is to explode, as a bomb does

indicators.note: the first stage of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rocket's first stage is set to blow outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first stage of rocket' sounds like a booster, but gives only R, which GO UP wraps 'outwardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection of things belonging together, a synonym for a cluster.

clue.text: Old mammoth hunter, or inhabitant of Norway, originally

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An ancient hunter of mammoths, or perhaps an early Norwegian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mammoth' reads as prehistoric beast, but it means huge: the giant hunter of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant hunter of Greek myth, now a constellation; mammoth here means enormous.

clue.text: Gay spark

definitions.meaning: gay in its older sense of lively, full of spirit
to spark is to bring to life, enliven

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means lively and spirited; as a verb it means to enliven or rouse into action.

clue.text: Fabric of the German state

definitions.meaning: a coarse jute cloth used for sacking
relating to Hesse, a state of Germany

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sacking cloth bears this name, as does anything belonging to Hesse in Germany.

clue.text: Faithful follower, for example, in story

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for story

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A loyal follower appears, for example, in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' looks like a tale, but here it is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times this was a vassal owing loyalty and service to a lord.

clue.text: A novelist in some hesitation — one from New York, perhaps

indicators.note: in places a and the novelist inside the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A novelist, hesitating somewhat, is a New Yorker.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne is the novelist. 'perhaps' marks New York as one example among eastern places.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the eastern part of a country, as New Yorkers are in America.
